column1: # The `--dns-suffix <suffix>` grammar's shared case table (app#510, #507 review-5x R1#1).
# `auth.<suffix>` default, the FALCO_CTF_DNS_SUFFIX env). The grammar is an RFC 1123
# subdomain, lower case (an Ingress host must be): labels of [a-z0-9-], the first and
# the last a letter or digit, 1 to 63 characters, joined by `.`, no leading or trailing
# dot, 253 characters in all. The 253 is deploy-user.sh's DNS_SUFFIX_MAX_LEN (a regex
# cannot count the whole), checked after the pattern; this table's rows hold it.
# The one Go definition of the grammar is internal/dnsname (ADR-0047); deploy-user.sh's
# DNS_SUFFIX_PATTERN / DNS_SUFFIX_MAX_LEN are a copy of it. The readers:
#   - Go:    internal/dnsname (dnsname_test.go) pins this header, the shell literal and
#            dnsname.Pattern equal, DNS_SUFFIX_MAX_LEN to dnsname.MaxLen = 253, and runs
#   - shell: charts/ctf-user/deploy-user.sh, run row by row as `--dns-suffix <input>` by
# An empty value has no row: `--dns-suffix ""` is the flag parser's usage error (exit 1).
# Format: the same as internal/identity/testdata/seat-cases.tsv (see its header):
# {U+00EF}, line 1 the canonical `# pattern: ` literal. The table stays ASCII.
# The input is the value as the operator gives it, with the one exception that an
# empty value has no row (see below). A row is never dropped to make an
# implementation pass: the implementation that disagrees is the bug.
# --- a value helm or YAML would type: valid DNS labels, which is why the value goes in with --set-string
# --- length: a label is at most 63, the whole at most 253
# --- each label starts and ends with a letter or digit
# --- no empty label, no leading or trailing dot
# --- lower case ASCII letters, digits and hyphen only
# --- helm --set syntax: a `,` starts another key, `=` another assignment
# --- line breaks, a bidi control, a non-ASCII letter
